newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia NSW state 96/97 budget on target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia NSW state 96/97 budget on target.

text.p: The New South Wales (NSW) state government on Friday it was still on target to meet a A$5 million surplus on its 1996/97 budget (to June 30) despite having to absorb two major and unexpected shocks.
The NSW Treasury said after analysis of the six months to December 1996 that the full year result had been revised to a deficit of A$5 million, a A$10 million downward adjustment.
State Treasurer Michael Egan said an estimated A$5 million deficit at the half-way mark in a A$23 billion budget could easily become a surplus by the end of the year.
"This year the Commonwealth (federal government) is slugging us for more than A$350 million through cuts to financial assistance grants and funding for health and roads," Egan said.

"And our rail reforms - where we separating freight and maintenance operations from passenger services and creasting a new authority to give private sector access to public track - have revealed a major cost to the budget," he added.
Egan said the corporatisation of Freight Rail had uncovered that the freight division of the SRA was used as a vehicle for borrowing money to fund commuter train services.

"Now that freight rail is an independent business - and off the budget - we've discovered it borrowed hundreds of millions of dollars it didn't need, money that was used to cross-subsidise passenger services," he said.
"It's bad news for the budget in the short term, but now we are addressing a problem that's remained hidden for years," the Treasurer added.
The Treasurer said the full year result predicted in this year's report was almost "bang-on" the budget-time estimate, unlike either of the previous two years.
The report showed that the projected A$10 million deterioration in the underlying result was due to a A$430 million increase in current outlays.
The main factors contributing to this increase were an additions A$205 million in health outlays and a funding shortfall in rail services accounting for A$205 million.
Current receipts increased A$286 million net of the A$209 million "Special Revenue Assistance" payments to the state was required to make to the Commonwealth, he said.

The A$107 million deterioration in the headline result, relative to budget includes an increase in costs associated with the sale of State Bank and the exclusion of State Bank and Axiom sale transactions from the underlying result, the report added.
